**Northgate Logistics: from a monthly release to forty deploys a week**

Northgate Logistics writes route-planning software for freight brokers. Through early 2024 the team shipped on the third Thursday of each month. Release night ran past midnight, two people sat on call, and about one release in four got rolled back.

"We weren't slow, exactly," says Dana Okafor, VP of Engineering. "Every release carried three weeks of changes piled on each other. When something broke, nobody could say which change broke it."

Northgate switched to a continuous delivery platform in March 2024. The move took a quarter, and most of that was not pipeline work. The first six weeks went into the test suite, which ran for 90 minutes and still let through code that failed in production. Once it finished in under eight minutes, automatic promotion from staging to production became worth trusting.

A year later:

- Deploys rose from one a month to roughly 40 a week
- Change failure rate fell from 24% to 3%
- Median time from merge to production dropped from 23 days to 51 minutes
- Rollback takes one click and about four minutes

Okafor is careful about attribution. "The tooling did not fix our culture. It made small batches affordable, and small batches fixed plenty on their own."

Northgate is now trying progressive rollouts, sending a change to 5% of brokers before the rest see it.

---

Two notes if you adapt this. The "tests came before the pipeline" beat is what keeps it out of brochure territory, and the last quote hands the platform less credit than a vendor would. Both do real work. With a live customer, the number to dig for in the interview is the one that embarrassed them.
